zh: 三、明破魔法者，當用三法除却魔罪：一者、了知所見聞覺知皆無所有，不受不著，亦不憂慼，亦不分別，彼即不現。二者、但反觀能見聞覺知之心，不見生處，何所惱亂？如是觀時，不受不分別，便自謝滅。三者、若作此觀，不即去者，但當正念，勿生懼想，不著軀命，正心不動，知魔界如即是佛界如。魔界如、佛界如，一如無二如，於魔界無所捨，於佛界無所取，即佛法現前，魔自退散。既不見去來，亦不憂喜，爾時豈為魔所惱？
en: Third, clarifying the methods for defeating demons: one should employ three methods to remove demonic offense.

First, understanding clearly that everything seen, heard, felt, and known has, in truth, nothing to it at all — neither receiving it nor becoming attached to it, neither troubled by it nor discriminating it — and it will not manifest at all.

Second, simply turning the contemplation back upon the very mind that sees, hears, feels, and knows, and finding no place where it truly arises — from what, then, could any disturbance possibly come? Contemplating in this way, neither receiving nor discriminating it, it will then pass away and vanish of itself.

Third, if, having made this contemplation, it still fails to depart at once, one should simply hold to right mindfulness, giving rise to no fear, unattached even to one's own body and life, the mind kept correct and unmoving, knowing that the suchness of the demon's realm is precisely the very same suchness as the buddha's realm. The suchness of the demon's realm and the suchness of the buddha's realm are one and the same suchness, with no second suchness apart from it — within the demon's realm there is nothing to reject, and within the buddha's realm there is nothing to grasp; the Buddhadharma then manifests directly before one, and the demon retreats and scatters of itself. Once one no longer sees any coming or going, and is neither troubled nor delighted by it, how, then, could one possibly still be troubled by the demon at all?

zh: 復次，亦未曾見有人坐中見魔作虎來剩食此人，骨肉狼藉，正是怖人，令心驚畏耳，都無實事，當知虛誑。如是知已，心不驚怖。復作是念：「設令是實，我今身命為道故死，何足可懼？今我此身，隨汝分別，心如金剛，不可迴轉。」如是或一月、二月，乃至經年不去，亦當端心，正念堅固，莫懷憂懼，當誦大乘方等諸治魔呪，默念誦之，存心三寶。若出禪定，亦當誦呪自防，懺悔慚悚，及誦波羅提木叉戒，邪不干正，久久自滅。事理除魔，其法眾多，非可備說，行者善須識之，方便除滅。故初心行人欲學坐時，必須親近善知識者，為有如此等難。是魔入人心時，能令行人證諸禪定、三昧、智慧、神通、陀羅尼，何況不能作此小小境界？若欲知之，諸大乘經及《九十六種道經》中，亦少分分別。今略說此，為令行者深知此意，則不妄受諸境。
en: Furthermore: no one has ever actually been seen, while sitting, to have a demon truly appear as a tiger and devour them, flesh and bone scattered about — this is simply meant to frighten a person, causing the mind to startle and fear; there is, in truth, no real matter to it at all, and one should know it to be empty and false. Knowing this, the mind is no longer startled or afraid. One should further reflect: "Even should this be real, I have already given this body and life for the sake of the path — why, then, should it be feared at all? Let this body of mine now be however you would have it — my mind is like vajra, and cannot be turned back." Even should it persist in this way for a month, two months, or even a full year without departing, one should still keep the mind upright, right mindfulness held firm, harboring no worry or fear, reciting the various Mahāyāna Vaipulya mantras for treating demons, silently reciting them, keeping the mind fixed on the Triple Gem. Upon emerging from concentration, one should likewise recite mantras to protect oneself, feeling shame and remorse in repentance, and recite the prātimokṣa precepts as well — deviance cannot interfere with the correct, and, over time, it will vanish of itself.

The methods for removing demons, in terms of both phenomenal practice and underlying principle, are themselves manifold and cannot be given here in full; the practitioner must properly recognize them, and remove them through skillful means. Hence a beginning practitioner wishing to learn sitting meditation must draw close to a wise teacher, precisely because of difficulties such as these. When this demon enters into a person's mind, it is able to make the practitioner realize the various dhyāna-concentrations, samādhis, wisdom, supernormal powers, and dhāraṇīs — how much more, then, could it fail to produce these lesser, trivial states as well? Should one wish to know more of this, the various Mahāyāna sūtras and the Sūtra of the Ninety-Six Paths distinguish it in some small part as well. This is given here only in brief, so that the practitioner may deeply understand this point, and thereby not carelessly accept any such state at face value.

zh:
取要言之，若欲遣邪歸正，當觀諸法實相。是故《摩訶衍論》云：「除諸法實相，其餘一切皆是魔事。」故偈言：
若分別憶想，是即魔羅網。
不動不分別，是即為法印。
常念常空理，是人非行道，
不生不滅中，而作分別想。
en:
To state the essential point: if one wishes to dispel the deviant and return to the correct, one should contemplate the true mark of all dharmas. Hence the Mahāyāna treatise says: "Apart from the true mark of all dharmas, everything else whatsoever is demonic affairs." Hence the verse says:
"If one discriminates and gives rise to deluded thought, this is precisely Māra's own net;
Unmoving and free of discrimination, this is precisely the Dharma-seal.
One who is forever mindful of the principle of emptiness, and yet
Still gives rise to discriminating thought within what neither arises nor ceases — this person is not truly walking the path."

zh: 復次，略明破魔義不同，如《摩訶衍》中說：「得菩薩道故，破煩惱魔；得法性身故，破陰界入魔；得菩薩道，得法性身故，破死魔；得不動三昧，一切法中自在無住故，破欲界他化自在天子魔。」若《大集經》，明得四念處即破四魔。此二說，名異意同。若《纓絡經》，明等覺如來三魔已過，唯有一品死魔在。若《法華》說，二乘之人但破三魔，餘有欲界天子魔所未能破。此則經論互說不同，悉有深意。若通明四魔，並至菩提方盡。
en: Furthermore: the sense in which demons are defeated differs somewhat depending on the source. As the Mahāyāna treatise says: "Through attaining the bodhisattva path, the demon of affliction is defeated; through attaining the dharma-nature body, the demon of the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements is defeated; through attaining both the bodhisattva path and the dharma-nature body, the demon of death is defeated; through attaining the unmoving samādhi, free and unattached within every dharma, the demon of the desire realm's Heavenly Son is defeated." The Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra clarifies that attaining the four foundations of mindfulness defeats all four demons at once — these two accounts differ in name but agree in sense. The Yingluo Sūtra clarifies that the Tathāgata at the stage of equal enlightenment has already passed beyond three of the demons, with only a single remaining grade of the demon of death still present. The Lotus Sūtra says that followers of the two lesser vehicles defeat only three of the demons, the demon of the desire realm's Heavenly Son alone remaining undefeated by them. These sūtras and treatises thus differ from one another in what they say, each carrying its own profound intent. Speaking generally of all four demons together, they are, in every case, only fully exhausted upon reaching bodhi itself.

zh: 所以者何？如煩惱魔，無明細惑，佛菩提智之所能斷。陰界入魔，如告憍陳如：「色是無常，因滅是色，獲得常色。受、想、行、識亦復如是。」死魔，如前取《纓絡經》所說。欲界天子魔，坐道場時，方來與菩薩興大鬪戰。故知四魔皆至菩提究竟永盡。菩薩摩訶薩心廣大故，安住不動，修深禪定，從初發心乃至佛果，降伏四魔而作佛事，廣化眾生，心不退沒。《涅槃經》中說有八魔，《華嚴經》中說有十魔，善得其意，四魔攝盡，更無別法。諸經辨魔事眾多，略說不具足。
en: Why is this? The demon of affliction — the subtle delusion of ignorance — can only be severed by the Buddha's own bodhi-wisdom. The demon of the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements is as the Buddha told Kauṇḍinya: "Form is impermanent; through the cessation of this form, a permanent form is attained. Sensation, perception, formations, and consciousness are exactly the same." The demon of death is as already cited above from the Yingluo Sūtra. The demon of the desire realm's Heavenly Son comes to wage great battle against the bodhisattva only at the very moment of sitting at the seat of enlightenment itself. Hence it is known that all four demons are only ever brought to their final, eternal end upon reaching bodhi.

Because the mahāsattva bodhisattva's mind is vast and expansive, abiding unmoved, cultivating profound dhyāna-concentration from the very first arising of the resolve all the way through to the fruit of buddhahood, subduing the four demons while carrying out the Buddha's own work, broadly transforming sentient beings, the mind never regressing or sinking. The Nirvāṇa Sūtra speaks of eight demons, and the Avataṃsaka Sūtra speaks of ten demons; properly grasping their sense, all are fully encompassed within these same four demons, with no separate dharma apart from them. The various sūtras' discussions of demonic affairs are themselves manifold; this is only given here in brief, not in full.

The three methods for defeating demons trace the exact same coarse-to-fine escalation this treatise has used repeatedly since fascicle 3: first a direct refusal to engage (neither receiving nor discriminating what appears), then turning analysis back on the perceiving mind itself, and, only if the first two fail, the "suchness of the demon's realm is precisely the suchness of the buddha's realm" — the identical move embodying-truth stopping and the vajra wheel already made, dissolving the demon/buddha distinction rather than defeating one side of it. The closing survey — different sūtras crediting different attainments with defeating different demons, none of them actually contradicting each other once "each carrying its own profound intent" is taken seriously — is a fitting close to the entire internal expedient means: even total victory over the four demons is deferred all the way to buddhahood itself, so a practitioner still deep in this fascicle's earlier layers should expect ongoing struggle, not a clean finish line. This closes recognizing demonic affairs, the fifth and final internal-expedient-means layer, the whole of topic 6 (the twenty-five preliminary conditions and the internal expedient means together), and fascicle 4.

quiz.q: In the third method of defeating demons, what should one know?
options: the suchness of the demon's realm is the suchness of the buddha's realm, one without a second; nothing to reject or grasp, the Dharma manifests and the demon scatters
quiz.why: "One should simply hold to right mindfulness, giving rise to no fear ... knowing that the suchness of the demon's realm is precisely the very same suchness as the buddha's realm ... within the demon's realm there is nothing to reject, and within the buddha's realm there is nothing to grasp; the Buddhadharma then manifests directly before one, and the demon retreats and scatters of itself."
